people.name: Adam
people.summary: The first man, formed by God from the dust and made in his image. Through his disobedience sin and death entered the world; Paul calls Christ the last Adam, through whom comes life.

people.name: Eve
people.summary: The first woman, made from Adam's side as a helper fit for him. After the fall God promised that her offspring would crush the serpent's head (Genesis 3:15), the first promise of the gospel.

people.name: Cain
people.summary: Adam and Eve's firstborn, a farmer. In jealousy he murdered his brother Abel, and went away from the presence of the LORD to the land of Nod.

people.name: Abel
people.summary: A shepherd whose offering God accepted. Killed by his brother, he is the first martyr: "through his faith, though he died, he still speaks".

people.name: Seth
people.summary: Born after Abel's death, "another offspring instead of Abel". In his son's days people began to call on the name of the LORD.

meaning.text: Appointed: "God has appointed for me another offspring"

people.name: Enosh
people.summary: Seth's son. "At that time people began to call upon the name of the LORD."

people.name: Kenan
people.summary: Son of Enosh, in the line from Adam to Noah.

people.name: Mahalalel
people.summary: Son of Kenan, in the line from Adam to Noah.

people.name: Jared
people.summary: Son of Mahalalel and father of Enoch. The longest-lived man after Methuselah.

people.name: Enoch
people.summary: "Enoch walked with God, and he was not, for God took him." He did not see death. Jude quotes his prophecy of the Lord's coming in judgement.
people.note: He lived 365 years on earth before God took him.

people.name: Methuselah
people.summary: Son of Enoch and the longest-lived person in the Bible. By the ages in Genesis 5 he died in the year of the flood.

people.name: Lamech
people.summary: Father of Noah, who named his son in hope that he would bring relief from the curse on the ground.
people.note: Not the same as Lamech of Cain's line (Genesis 4:18-24).

people.name: Noah
people.summary: "Noah found favour in the eyes of the LORD." A righteous man in a corrupt generation, he built the ark by faith and was saved with his family through the flood. God made his covenant with Noah and every living creature, with the rainbow as its sign.

meaning.text: Rest: "this one shall bring us relief"

people.name: Shem
people.summary: Noah's son, blessed by his father: "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem." Ancestor of Eber, Abraham and the Semitic peoples.

people.name: Ham
people.summary: Noah's son, father of Cush, Egypt, Put and Canaan, the peoples of Africa and Canaan in the Table of Nations.

people.name: Japheth
people.summary: Noah's son, ancestor of the peoples of the coastlands and the north, including the Greeks (Javan) and Medes (Madai).

people.name: Canaan
people.summary: Ham's son, cursed by Noah after Ham's sin. His descendants were the Canaanite peoples whose land God later gave to Israel.

people.name: Arphaxad
people.summary: Born two years after the flood.
people.note: Luke 3:36 names Cainan between Arphaxad and Shelah, following the Greek Septuagint. Genesis 11 in Hebrew does not.

people.name: Shelah
people.summary: In the line from Shem to Abraham.

people.name: Eber
people.summary: Ancestor from whom the name "Hebrew" may come. Shem is called "the father of all the children of Eber".

people.name: Peleg
people.summary: "In his days the earth was divided", perhaps referring to the scattering of the nations at Babel.

people.name: Reu
people.summary: In the line from Shem to Abraham.

people.name: Serug
people.summary: In the line from Shem to Abraham.

people.name: Nahor
people.summary: Abraham's grandfather.
people.note: Not the same as Abraham's brother Nahor.

people.name: Terah
people.summary: Abraham's father, who served other gods in Ur. He set out with his family for Canaan but settled and died in Haran.

people.name: Abraham
people.summary: Called by God from Ur to the land he would show him. He believed the LORD, who counted it to him as righteousness, and received the promise that in him all the families of the earth would be blessed. The father of all who believe.

people.name: Nahor
people.summary: Abraham's brother, who stayed in Mesopotamia. His granddaughter Rebekah married Isaac.

people.name: Haran
people.summary: Abraham's brother, who died in Ur. Father of Lot and Milcah.

people.name: Sarah
people.summary: Abraham's wife and half-sister, barren until God gave her Isaac at 90. Hebrews praises her faith, and Peter holds her up as a model for Christian wives.
people.note: Abraham calls her "the daughter of my father though not the daughter of my mother" (Genesis 20:12).

people.name: Hagar
people.summary: Sarah's Egyptian servant, given to Abraham as a wife. Twice in the wilderness the angel of the LORD found her and cared for her and her son.

people.name: Keturah
people.summary: Abraham's wife after Sarah's death, mother of six sons including Midian.

people.name: Lot
people.summary: Abraham's nephew, who chose the Jordan valley and settled in Sodom. Rescued before its destruction, he is called "righteous Lot" by Peter.

people.name: Milcah
people.summary: Haran's daughter, who married her uncle Nahor. Grandmother of Rebekah.

people.name: Moab
people.summary: Son of Lot by his elder daughter, ancestor of the Moabites, the people of Ruth.

people.name: Ben-ammi
people.summary: Son of Lot by his younger daughter, ancestor of the Ammonites.

people.name: Ishmael
people.summary: Abraham's son by Hagar. God heard him and made him a great nation, father of twelve princes, but the covenant was established with Isaac.

people.name: Isaac
people.summary: The son of promise, born when Abraham was 100. Bound on the altar at Moriah and spared when God provided a ram, he inherited the covenant promises.

people.name: Midian
people.summary: Son of Abraham and Keturah, ancestor of the Midianites. Moses married into a Midianite family.

people.name: Bethuel
people.summary: Son of Nahor and Milcah, father of Rebekah and Laban.

people.name: Rebekah
people.summary: Chosen in answer to the prayer of Abraham's servant, she left her family to marry Isaac. She was told "the older shall serve the younger" before Esau and Jacob were born.

people.name: Laban
people.summary: Rebekah's brother in Haran, who gave Jacob his daughters Leah and Rachel and repeatedly cheated him over twenty years.

people.name: Esau
people.summary: Jacob's older twin, a hunter, who sold his birthright for a meal. He forgave Jacob, settled in Seir and was the father of the Edomites.

people.name: Jacob
people.summary: The younger twin, chosen before birth. He took Esau's blessing by deceit, met God at Bethel, served Laban twenty years and wrestled with God at Peniel. His twelve sons became the tribes of Israel.

meaning.text: He takes by the heel; renamed Israel, "he strives with God"

people.name: Leah
people.summary: Laban's older daughter, given to Jacob by deception. Unloved, she was blessed by God with six sons, among them Levi and Judah, the ancestors of Israel's priests and kings.

people.name: Rachel
people.summary: Laban's younger daughter, whom Jacob loved and served fourteen years to marry. Long barren, she bore Joseph, and died giving birth to Benjamin near Bethlehem.

people.name: Bilhah
people.summary: Rachel's servant, given to Jacob. Mother of Dan and Naphtali.

people.name: Zilpah
people.summary: Leah's servant, given to Jacob. Mother of Gad and Asher.

people.name: Reuben
people.summary: Jacob's firstborn, who tried to rescue Joseph from his brothers. He lost the rights of the firstborn because he slept with his father's concubine.

people.name: Simeon
people.summary: One of the twelve sons of Jacob, ancestor of the tribe of Simeon. With Levi he avenged Dinah on Shechem. Joseph kept him in Egypt as a hostage.

people.name: Levi
people.summary: Jacob's third son. His descendants, the Levites, were set apart for the LORD's service, and from them came Moses, Aaron and the priests.

meaning.text: Attached: "my husband will be attached to me"

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Jacob's fourth son. He offered himself as a slave in Benjamin's place, and Jacob promised that "the sceptre shall not depart from Judah". From his tribe came David and Jesus, the Lion of the tribe of Judah.

meaning.text: Praise: "this time I will praise the LORD"

people.name: Issachar
people.summary: One of the twelve sons of Jacob, ancestor of the tribe of Issachar. Its men later "had understanding of the times".

people.name: Zebulun
people.summary: One of the twelve sons of Jacob, ancestor of the tribe of Zebulun. Isaiah foretold a great light in the land of Zebulun and Naphtali, fulfilled in Jesus' ministry in Galilee.

people.name: Dinah
people.summary: Jacob's daughter by Leah. Her violation by Shechem led to Simeon and Levi's revenge on the city.

people.name: Dan
people.summary: One of the twelve sons of Jacob, ancestor of the tribe of Dan. Samson was a Danite.

people.name: Naphtali
people.summary: One of the twelve sons of Jacob, ancestor of the tribe of Naphtali. Barak, who fought with Deborah, came from Naphtali.

people.name: Gad
people.summary: One of the twelve sons of Jacob, ancestor of the tribe of Gad. The tribe settled east of the Jordan.

people.name: Asher
people.summary: One of the twelve sons of Jacob, ancestor of the tribe of Asher. The prophetess Anna, who greeted the baby Jesus, was of this tribe.

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: Jacob's favoured son, sold into Egypt by his brothers. God raised him from slavery and prison to rule Egypt and save many lives in the famine: "You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good."

meaning.text: May he add: "may the LORD add to me another son"

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: Jacob's youngest son, the only one born in Canaan. His tribe gave Israel its first king, Saul, and the apostle Paul.

people.name: Asenath
people.summary: Joseph's Egyptian wife, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On.

people.name: Manasseh
people.summary: Joseph's firstborn, adopted by Jacob as one of his own sons. His tribe settled on both sides of the Jordan.

meaning.text: Making to forget: "God has made me forget all my hardship"

people.name: Ephraim
people.summary: Joseph's younger son, whom Jacob blessed ahead of his brother. Ephraim became the leading tribe of the north, and its name came to stand for the whole northern kingdom.

people.name: Joshua
people.summary: Son of Nun of the tribe of Ephraim. Moses' assistant and successor, he led Israel into the promised land: "As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD."

meaning.text: The LORD saves (the same name as Jesus)

people.note: 1 Chronicles 7:20-27 traces about ten generations from Ephraim to Joshua.

people.name: Kohath
people.summary: Levi's son. His clan, the Kohathites, carried the ark and the holy things of the tabernacle.

people.name: Amram
people.summary: Father of Miriam, Aaron and Moses.
people.note: Exodus 6 is usually read as naming the main ancestors rather than every generation across Israel's years in Egypt.

people.name: Jochebed
people.summary: A daughter of Levi, mother of Moses. By faith she hid her baby and set him among the reeds of the Nile.

people.name: Miriam
people.summary: Sister of Moses and Aaron. She watched over the baby Moses and led the women in song after the sea crossing. Micah names her among the leaders God sent.

people.name: Aaron
people.summary: Moses' older brother and spokesman, consecrated as Israel's first high priest. All later priests descended from him.

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn from the Nile and raised in Pharaoh's house, he met God at the burning bush and led Israel out of Egypt. Through him God gave the law. "There has not arisen a prophet since in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face."

meaning.text: Drawn out: "because I drew him out of the water"

people.name: Zipporah
people.summary: Daughter of Jethro (Reuel), priest of Midian, and wife of Moses.

people.name: Gershom
people.summary: Moses' firstborn, born in Midian.

meaning.text: A sojourner there: "I have been a sojourner in a foreign land"

people.name: Eliezer
people.summary: Moses' second son.

people.name: Elisheba
people.summary: Aaron's wife, daughter of Amminadab and sister of Nahshon of Judah, so the priestly line and the royal line were joined by marriage.

people.name: Nadab
people.summary: Aaron's firstborn, who with Abihu offered unauthorised fire before the LORD and died.

people.name: Abihu
people.summary: Aaron's son, who died with Nadab for offering unauthorised fire.

people.name: Eleazar
people.summary: Aaron's son and successor as high priest, who helped Joshua divide the land.

people.name: Ithamar
people.summary: Aaron's youngest son, who oversaw the Levites' work on the tabernacle. Eli the priest was probably descended from him.

people.name: Phinehas
people.summary: Eleazar's son, given "a covenant of a perpetual priesthood" for his zeal for the LORD at Peor.

people.name: Tamar
people.summary: Judah's daughter-in-law. Denied the son she was owed, she conceived by Judah himself, who admitted "she is more righteous than I". She is one of four women named in Jesus' genealogy in Matthew.

people.name: Perez
people.summary: Twin son of Judah and Tamar, who broke out ahead of his brother. Ancestor of David.

people.name: Zerah
people.summary: Twin brother of Perez, ancestor of Achan and of the wise men Ethan and Heman.

people.name: Hezron
people.summary: Son of Perez, who went down to Egypt with Jacob.

people.name: Ram
people.summary: In the line of Judah, from Perez to David.
people.note: The line from Hezron to Nahshon spans Israel's years in Egypt, so it probably names key ancestors rather than every generation.

people.name: Amminadab
people.summary: Father of Nahshon and of Elisheba, Aaron's wife.

people.name: Nahshon
people.summary: Leader of the tribe of Judah in the wilderness, who brought the first offering at the dedication of the tabernacle.

people.name: Salmon
people.summary: Husband of Rahab and father of Boaz.

people.name: Rahab
people.summary: A Canaanite prostitute of Jericho who hid Israel's spies because she feared the LORD. She was saved with her family, married into Judah and is named in Jesus' genealogy and among the heroes of faith.

people.name: Boaz
people.summary: A worthy man of Bethlehem who acted as kinsman-redeemer for Naomi's family and married Ruth: a picture of Christ the Redeemer.
people.note: Matthew 1:5 names Rahab as his mother. Since the conquest is about three centuries before David, Salmon and Boaz may stand for a longer line.

people.name: Ruth
people.summary: A Moabite widow who left her people for Naomi and her God: "Your people shall be my people, and your God my God." She married Boaz and became David's great-grandmother.

people.name: Obed
people.summary: Son of Boaz and Ruth, of whom the women of Bethlehem said "A son has been born to Naomi." Grandfather of David.

people.name: Jesse
people.summary: A Bethlehemite, father of eight sons, the youngest being David. Isaiah foretold "a shoot from the stump of Jesse".

people.name: Kish
people.summary: A Benjaminite of Gibeah, father of King Saul.

people.name: Saul
people.summary: Israel's first king, chosen and anointed by Samuel. He began well but disobeyed the LORD, who rejected him and chose David. He died with his sons on Mount Gilboa.

people.name: Jonathan
people.summary: Saul's son, a brave warrior and David's closest friend, who loved him as his own soul and gave up his claim to the throne.

people.name: Michal
people.summary: Saul's daughter, who loved David and saved his life. She later despised him for dancing before the ark, and had no children.

people.name: Mephibosheth
people.summary: Jonathan's son, lame in both feet, to whom David showed kindness for Jonathan's sake, giving him a place at the king's table.

people.name: David
people.summary: The shepherd boy anointed by Samuel, who killed Goliath and became Israel's greatest king, "a man after God's own heart". God promised that his throne would be established forever, a promise fulfilled in Jesus, the Son of David. He wrote many of the psalms.

people.name: Bathsheba
people.summary: Wife of Uriah the Hittite, taken by David in adultery. After David repented, she became the mother of Solomon and secured his succession. Matthew names her as "the wife of Uriah".

people.name: Amnon
people.summary: David's firstborn (by Ahinoam), who violated his half-sister Tamar and was killed by Absalom.

people.name: Absalom
people.summary: David's son (by Maacah), handsome and ambitious, who rebelled against his father and was killed. David mourned, "O my son Absalom!"

people.name: Adonijah
people.summary: David's son (by Haggith), who tried to seize the throne before Solomon was crowned.

people.name: Nathan
people.summary: A son of David and Bathsheba. Luke traces Jesus' genealogy through him.
people.note: Not the prophet Nathan. Luke 3 follows Nathan's line down to Heli; Matthew 1 follows Solomon's line down to Joseph. Many think Luke gives Mary's line and Matthew Joseph's legal, royal line; others think both trace Joseph, one by natural and one by legal descent.

people.name: Solomon
people.summary: David's son and successor, who asked God for wisdom and built the temple in Jerusalem. His many foreign wives turned his heart to other gods, and after his death the kingdom divided.

meaning.text: Peace; God named him Jedidiah, "beloved of the LORD"

people.name: Naamah
people.summary: An Ammonite wife of Solomon, mother of Rehoboam.

people.name: Rehoboam
people.summary: Solomon's son. His harsh answer to the people split the kingdom; he ruled only Judah and Benjamin.

people.name: Abijah
people.summary: King of Judah for three years.

people.name: Asa
people.summary: A reforming king of Judah who removed idols and relied on the LORD, though he later trusted in Aram and in doctors rather than God.

people.name: Jehoshaphat
people.summary: A godly king of Judah who sent teachers through the land with the Book of the Law, but allied himself with Ahab.

people.name: Athaliah
people.summary: Daughter of Ahab, wife of King Jehoram. After her son Ahaziah's death she killed the royal family and seized the throne, but the infant Joash was hidden and later crowned.

people.name: Jehoram
people.summary: King of Judah who married Ahab's daughter and walked in the ways of Israel's kings.

people.name: Ahaziah
people.summary: King of Judah for one year, killed by Jehu.

people.name: Joash
people.summary: Hidden as a baby from Athaliah and crowned at seven, he repaired the temple while the priest Jehoiada guided him, but later turned away.

people.name: Amaziah
people.summary: King of Judah who defeated Edom, then worshipped Edom's gods and was defeated by Israel.

people.name: Uzziah
people.summary: A long-reigning, successful king of Judah, struck with leprosy when he proudly burned incense in the temple. Isaiah saw the Lord in the year he died.

people.name: Jotham
people.summary: A king of Judah who did right in the eyes of the LORD.

people.name: Ahaz
people.summary: An idolatrous king of Judah who refused Isaiah's offer of a sign and appealed to Assyria. To him Isaiah gave the sign of the virgin's son, Immanuel.

people.name: Hezekiah
people.summary: One of Judah's greatest kings, who trusted the LORD, reformed worship and was delivered from the Assyrian army of Sennacherib.

people.name: Manasseh
people.summary: Judah's longest-reigning and most wicked king, who filled Jerusalem with idols and innocent blood. Chronicles records that he humbled himself in exile and was restored.

people.name: Amon
people.summary: An evil king of Judah, murdered by his servants after two years.

people.name: Josiah
people.summary: Crowned at eight, he sought the LORD, found the Book of the Law in the temple and led a great reform. No king before or after turned to the LORD with all his heart as he did.

people.name: Jehoahaz
people.summary: Josiah's son, who reigned three months before Pharaoh Neco took him to Egypt.

people.name: Jehoiakim
people.summary: Josiah's son, put on the throne by Egypt. He burned Jeremiah's scroll and rebelled against Babylon.

people.name: Zedekiah
people.summary: Josiah's son and Judah's last king. He rebelled against Babylon, and Jerusalem and the temple were destroyed in his eleventh year.

people.name: Jehoiachin
people.summary: King for three months before he was taken captive to Babylon. Released from prison there 37 years later, he ate at the king of Babylon's table.

people.name: Shealtiel
people.summary: Son of Jehoiachin, born in exile.

people.name: Zerubbabel
people.summary: Governor of Judah who led the first return from Babylon and rebuilt the temple. God called him his signet ring.
people.note: Usually called the son of Shealtiel; 1 Chronicles 3:19 names his father as Pedaiah, Shealtiel's brother, perhaps through a levirate marriage.

people.name: Abiud
people.summary: Named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus between the return from exile and Joseph. Nothing else is known of him.

people.name: Eliakim
people.summary: Named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus between the return from exile and Joseph. Nothing else is known of him.
people.note: Not the same as others of this name in the Old Testament.

people.name: Azor
people.summary: Named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus between the return from exile and Joseph. Nothing else is known of him.

people.name: Zadok
people.summary: Named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus between the return from exile and Joseph. Nothing else is known of him.
people.note: Not the same as others of this name in the Old Testament.

people.name: Achim
people.summary: Named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus between the return from exile and Joseph. Nothing else is known of him.

people.name: Eliud
people.summary: Named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus between the return from exile and Joseph. Nothing else is known of him.

people.name: Eleazar
people.summary: Named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus between the return from exile and Joseph. Nothing else is known of him.
people.note: Not the same as others of this name in the Old Testament.

people.name: Matthan
people.summary: Named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus between the return from exile and Joseph. Nothing else is known of him.

people.name: Jacob
people.summary: Named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus between the return from exile and Joseph. Nothing else is known of him.
people.note: Not the same as others of this name in the Old Testament.

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: A righteous carpenter of Nazareth, of the house of David, betrothed to Mary. Told by an angel that her child was conceived by the Holy Spirit, he took her as his wife and named the child Jesus, becoming his legal father.
people.note: Luke 3:23 calls Joseph "the son of Heli". See the note on Nathan for the two genealogies.

people.name: Mary
people.summary: The virgin of Nazareth chosen to bear the Son of God: "Behold, I am the servant of the Lord." She was at the cross and with the disciples in prayer after the ascension.

people.name: Jesus
people.summary: The eternal Son of God, born of the virgin Mary, the promised offspring of Eve, Abraham and David. He lived without sin, died for sinners, rose from the dead and reigns forever. In him all the promises of God find their Yes.

meaning.text: The LORD saves: "he will save his people from their sins"

people.note: Joseph was his legal father, not his natural father: Jesus was conceived by the Holy Spirit (Matthew 1:18-20; Luke 1:35).

people.name: Zechariah
people.summary: A priest of the division of Abijah, who was struck mute for doubting the angel's message until his son John was born.
people.note: A descendant of Aaron through the priestly divisions of 1 Chronicles 24.

people.name: Elizabeth
people.summary: A relative of Mary, "of the daughters of Aaron", who conceived John in her old age. Filled with the Holy Spirit, she called Mary "the mother of my Lord".

people.name: John the Baptist
people.summary: The forerunner who prepared the way for the Lord, baptised Jesus and pointed to him: "Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!"
